title: Explore several solutions before choosing one
summary: The first idea is rarely the best. Generate several different ways to solve the problem, compare them, and only then pick one to develop.

beginner: Reread the problem statement and success metrics with the team.
Turn the problem into 'How might we...' questions, for example 'How might we help new customers finish setup in one sitting?'
Run a session where everyone sketches ideas on their own first, then shares. Aim for quantity.
Group similar ideas and pick three that are genuinely different.
Compare the three on user value, effort, risk and fit with the metrics.
Choose one or two to prototype, and record why you set the others aside.
intermediate: Frame 'How might we' questions from the problem statement.
Run a divergent ideation session, with solo sketching before group discussion.
Shortlist at least three distinct concepts and compare them against agreed criteria.
Select concepts to prototype and record the reasoning.
experienced: Push the team beyond incremental ideas by including at least one bold option and one 'do less' option.
Involve engineering early so technical insight shapes the options.
Compare concepts using evidence and the four risks, not opinion or seniority.
Keep discarded options on file; they are often useful later.

canDelegateTo.task: Facilitate the ideation session and sketch concepts
Bring technical options and constraints to the session
Explore how each concept would be explained to users

toolExamples.miro: Use a crazy eights template: each person sketches eight ideas in eight minutes.
toolExamples.figma: Lay the shortlisted concepts side by side on one page for comparison.
toolExamples.mural: Run silent dot voting on concepts after everyone has presented.
toolExamples.claude: Describe the problem and ask for ten very different solution ideas, including some that use no technology.

definitionOfDone: At least three distinct concepts explored
pitfalls: Going with the first idea or the most senior person's idea
Generating variations of one idea instead of different ideas
Leaving engineers out until the design is finished

sources.title: Framework for innovation: the Double Diamond (Design Council)
Parallel and iterative design (Nielsen Norman Group)
